newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rises but IPB falls back at fixing.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rises but IPB falls back at fixing.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index rose at Monday's fixing led by the most heavily capitalised share, SPT Telecom which gained 109 crowns, 2.9 percent, to 3,750.
In contrast, the third most heavily capitalised banking issue, IPB Bank, which on Monday announced lower first half profits, lost seven crowns, 2.7 percent, to 255.

IPB said its first half net profits had slumped to 445 million crowns from 830 million in the same period in 1996. IPB added that its classified loans represented 19.6 percent of the total, almost unchanged from the first half of 1996.

IPB posted solid gains late last week in the wake of an announcement by the Finance Ministry that it would sell the state's 36 perecnt stake in the bank to Japan's Nomura Securities Co Ltd International for around six billion crowns.

Elsewhere, Komercni Banka rose 29 crowns to 1,645 and Ceska Sporitelna gained two crowns to 261. The Finance Ministry will present plans to the government for the further privatisation of the above two banks on August 20.
